s1.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic neurological syndrome with abdominal pain, vomiting, and altered mental status
salient_findings: Diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact
Frontal headache and persistent nausea after the episode
key_facts: 8-year-old boy with no significant past medical history
30-minute history of generalized abdominal pain
Single episode of vomiting
Developed diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact
Episode lasted 10 minutes
Reported a frontal headache (5/10) and persistent nausea after the episode
Family denied toxin or medication exposure
Similar episode 18 months earlier
No personal or family history of epilepsy or neurological disorders
Developmental milestones were age-appropriate
Normal vital signs except for blood pressure above the 95th percentile for age
Neurologic examination revealed confusion and disorientation
Normal motor and sensory examinations
Consciousness and orientation improved approximately 20 minutes after arrival
Three additional self-limited vomiting episodes and ongoing headache
Headache improved after a single IV dose of diclofenac (1 mg/kg)
Normal complete blood count, serum chemistries, and electrolytes
Normal brain MRI with an epilepsy protocol
